$comment: Clio's spoken phrase catalog — the single authored source.
Edit this file, then run `node voice/generate-voice-lines.mjs` to
regenerate the per-project copies and the audio. Do not edit the
generated files in client/ or mobile/ directly; CI checks them against
this one and fails on drift, because the two hand-maintained catalogs
this replaced had already diverged (mobile carried two duplicate keys
that web did not).
Keys are the contract both clients call by name. Each is a list of
variants; one is chosen at random so repetition doesn't grate on a child
hearing it twenty times an afternoon.
The ElevenLabs voice Clio speaks with. Changing it means regenerating
all audio. This is a brand asset, not a config value — audition before
settling.
`voiceId` is Alice (Clear, Engaging Educator), British, premade. The
voice we actually want is Sophia jB2lPb5DhAX6l1TLkKXy, but she is a
library voice and the API refuses those on a free plan with 402.
`modelId` is eleven_v3 because it performs [tags] as direction; the
turbo models read them out loud instead.

$comment: Whole lines spoken verbatim somewhere in the product, pre-generated so
they use Clio’s real voice instead of the browser synthesiser.
These are the scripted lesson on /about-eudora. That demo is the first
time most visitors hear her, and mixing a recorded voice for the praise
with a robotic one for the explanation is worse than either alone.
Matched on the exact string at playback time, so editing a line here
without regenerating simply falls back — it never plays the wrong audio.
lines: Let's show a fraction by colouring in part of a shape.
Hi, I'm Clio. Percent just means 'out of a hundred', so let's look at one.
Grids are just directions. Across first, then up.
Same idea as the shaded shape, written a different way.
Last one, and this time there's nothing to pick from.
Shade two of the six slices, so two sixths of the circle is coloured in.
Move the slider to show what percentage of this shape is shaded.
Clio buried her treasure 2 steps across and 4 steps up. Click that spot on the grid.
Maya cuts a pizza into 4 equal slices and eats 1 slice. Which fraction shows how much she ate?
Slide to show how many legs 3 dogs have altogether.
There are six equal slices in the circle. You only need to colour two of them in.
The shape has 10 equal squares, so one square is one tenth, and one tenth is 10%.
Walk along the bottom line first and stop at 2. Only then start climbing.
Start with the bottom number. It's how many equal slices the whole pizza was cut into.
One dog has 4 legs. Try counting up by 4, three times.
Two of the six equal slices are shaded, so the shape shows two sixths — that's 2/6 of the circle.
10 equal squares means each one is worth 10%. Three of them are shaded, so 3 × 10% = 30%.
Across before up, every time. 2 along the bottom and 4 up from there is the point (2, 4).
The bottom number counts the equal pieces in the whole (4 slices). The top counts how many were taken (1 slice). So Maya ate 1/4 of the pizza.
3 groups of 4 legs is 4 + 4 + 4, which is 12. That's what 3 × 4 means.
